summary: In this story, two cousins build homemade dune buggies for a friendly neighborhood race, learning about friction and gears along the way, and showing good sportsmanship when the race does not go as planned.
introduce: Show the title “The Race of the Dune Buggies” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: a force that slows things down when two surfaces rub together
connected wheels with teeth that change how much force is needed to move something
having a strong will to keep trying and not give up

challengeTerms.def: the force that keeps a moving object going
a set of connected parts that work together inside a machine
cleverness and skill in solving problems or inventing things

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that winning a race matters more than being a good sport about losing? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how friction affected the cousins' buggies, and how they solved the problem.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review friction, gears, and determined, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses momentum, mechanism, and ingenuity to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
